title: Canonical maps for scalar derived external cup of algebraic-space structure modules
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work with algebraic spaces over S and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the fixed small module and derived categories, degree-zero structure object and actual Zariski restriction [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction], and their representative-normalized ringed tensor/unit structure [def-zl-ringed-site-duality-model]. For a commutative ring A, an affine Y in Over(S) with e:Y≅Spec(A), and f:X→Y, put K_X=RΓ_A(X,O_X) using [def-sfb-space-affine-global-sections]. Define its multiplication as that node's relative scalar cup followed by O-multiplication, and its unit by local scalar multiplication a↦a id_O and the universal right-derived unit. Normalize the equivalence between Hom(O,-) sections and compatible-chart sections on every chart and by the right-derived units [def-sfb-space-affine-hom-comparison], [def-sfb-space-affine-sections-compositors]. With such normalized presentation witnesses, define pullback on K by the ordinary regular-function structure map, its small-model transport and canonical degree-zero-to-derived insertion [def-sfb-space-small-structure-derived-comparison], and the direct-image compositor [def-sfb-space-module-structure-map]; over a fixed affine base remove identity coefficient restriction by its canonical comparison. For a commuting cone W→X,Y define κ as tensor of these two projection pullbacks followed by multiplication, without assuming its invertibility. Define flat qcqs admissibility using the existing chartwise flatness and quasi-compactness of the structure map and its diagonal [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Retain the native derived Koszul symmetry. For an affine base morphism g:Y'→Y inducing a:A→B, define the B-linear comparison E_a K_X→K_X' as the scalar-adjoint of this geometric pullback, using the canonical derived scalar adjunction [def-zl-ring-derived-scalar-extension], [def-sfb-module-derived-scalar-comparisons]. Define scalar tensor presentation witnesses, natural in both derived arguments, by identifying E_a K⊗E_a L with E_a(K⊗L) and 1_B with E_a 1_A, fixed on flat-term K-flat representatives by ordinary scalar extension, its total tensor map, and localization. Define restriction tensor by taking the mate of this tensor comparison followed by the two scalar counits. Define coefficient identity and composition comparisons by ordinary restriction and uniqueness of its left adjoint. If X is represented by a scheme Z, use its actual ringed Zariski site and derived tensor as a ringed tensor corner and model [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-square-presentation]. A Zariski comparison witness consists of the representative-normalized tensor model, the scalar map A→Γ(Z,O_Z) fixed on every open by (g e)^*, the ordinary comparison on sections with actual restriction to opens, its derived comparison fixed by the universal derived units, and the structure comparison O_Z→Rε_*O_etale fixed on every regular function. Require the latter to be invertible, as in the quasi-coherent site comparison. The Zariski scalar multiplication is the existing global derived module cup [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product], [def-sfb-ringed-site-global-derived-adjunction] followed by O-multiplication and canonical restriction of scalars. The etale-to-Zariski scalar comparison is the derived section comparison followed by the inverse of that fixed structure comparison. These are definitions of the canonical maps and their normalized presentation data; no Kunneth, algebra, or base-change-coherence assertion is included.

lean.note: The external map is the primary construction; all accompanying maps and normalized witnesses are listed in declarations. Definitions contain real data and no sorry. Existence of the simultaneous normalized witnesses, along with all asserted laws, belongs to the consuming theorem.
